title: Testing your offer before you charge full price
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Run a small paid or free pilot with written terms
Collect feedback and evidence that the offer works
Update the offer and move to full pricing

instruction.heading: Iterate, do not guess
instruction.body: Your first offer will change. The only reliable way to improve it is to deliver it to real customers and listen. Start now, with a small number of jobs.

instruction.heading: Pilot with written terms
instruction.body: Offer a limited pilot, for example five jobs at a reduced rate or free in return for feedback and a written testimonial. Put the scope, the time, what you need from the customer, and what happens if the result is not met into a short written agreement.

instruction.heading: Collect evidence
instruction.body: Record photos before and after, the time taken, what went wrong, and the customer comments. Ask for a short review you can publish with consent.

instruction.heading: Move to full pricing
instruction.body: Update the offer from the feedback, then offer the same service at full price to the pilot customers first, and then to new customers. Note which price and scope they accept.

procedure: Define a pilot scope, number of jobs and the terms in writing.
Record time, photos and issues on every job.
Ask each customer for specific feedback and permission to publish a review.
Change the offer once the same issue appears on two jobs.
Move to full pricing and record acceptance.

workedExamples.situation: After three pilot cleans, the cleaner finds that bathrooms take 90 minutes longer than planned, and customers wanted a fixed time window.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should change before full pricing?
workedExamples.reasoning: Update the scope and the time estimate to match the evidence, then price the fixed window. Do not keep the old price for the new scope.

commonErrors.error: Running a pilot with no written scope, so disputes cannot be resolved
commonErrors.prevention: Put the pilot terms in writing before the first job.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring feedback because it is uncomfortable
commonErrors.prevention: Change the offer when the same problem appears twice.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state or territory rules before acting.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Pilot with written terms and record evidence.
Change the offer from feedback before charging full price.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a pilot have written terms?
options: To avoid paying tax on the pilot income for the year
To make the customer sign a contract for life and pay for it
Because the law requires it for every job and the lawyer checks it
So scope, time and remedies are clear if there is a dispute

knowledgeChecks.question: When should you change the offer?
options: When the same problem appears on two jobs
After the first job, before any second result is seen
Only when a competitor changes theirs
